$doc.purpose: A browser walked the create flow on the demo instance and wrote down every screen. Committed so a reviewer, and the /how-it-works replay (#898 card 2), can read what happened without re-running it.

topLevel.$doc: this block — the schema, in the file it describes
topLevel.base: the origin the walk ran against
topLevel.paths: one entry per path: { path, terminal (the screen the path must end on, in words), reached, steps }
topLevel.findings: behaviour the walk met that is not this driver's to fix: { n, path, title, shot, expected, actual, note }. A finding is a report, never a failure.
topLevel.steps: every screen, in order — see fields
topLevel.seed: what the run did about the demo dataset: { attempted, ok?, reason?, drift? }
topLevel.summary: what this run found: { paths, reached, steps, findings }
topLevel.cleanup: the branch before and after the walk: { created, before, after, leftover, unchanged }

fields.path: create-published | create-draft | unpaid — a state, not a happy path
fields.route: where the step happened; run-specific ids are normalised to <instance> and <token>
fields.values: verbatim what was entered; {} for clicks and asserts
fields.expect: the assertion this step proved, in words
fields.ok: whether it held; `actual` carries what was measured when it did not
fields.actual: only present when ok is false
fields.sha256: the digest of the image this run wrote — evidence of the run, not an invariant

$doc.determinism: steps and paths carry no timestamp, id or absolute path, and two runs on an unchanged tree write them identically — that is what `pnpm demo:flow:check` diffs, byte for byte. `summary`, `seed`, `cleanup` and each step's `sha256` are measurements of one run or of a shared branch, so the diff excludes them: screenshots are compared by the geometry in `w`/`h`, because a page prints a minted invitation token, mounts the provider's live frame and seeds placeholder art from a row's id — none of which is byte-stable.
